items.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: So I mentioned that to him when he was here at one of our clubs a few years back.

ctx.x: lead alto players in the country. His brother, Ernie Royal, outstanding trumpet player who ended up in New York doing studio work, but they all were with the original Lionel Hampton band, the band that made “Flying Home.” Vernon Alley of course, Mister Music, he was in the band, Wilbert Baranco, who is mentioned in the Leonard Feather, who was a very fine musician/pianist/singer and arranger. Wilbert, during the WPA days, he had been connected with the music project in San Francisco, and he wrote for everything,…

three years at St. Mary’s College. See we went in, when they called us we were all put on temporary leave when they first recruited us. Then when they told us okay it’s time, then we got on the train and this was in 1945 [sic] around October, maybe the first of October, yeah, got on the train, the Western Pacific, and took off for Chicago. Well there was a jam session going on where the guys had their books out and they were having jam sessions on the train. Because we had a private car. And they had one…
Boy that name has come up a lot, that place near Chicago where all the servicemen—
